hypothesis: Strike-aligned corridor emission with DEM slope concordance (tectonic-geomorphology lane — H63-A)
mechanism: Channel profiles record base-level steps across active normal faults. This emission combines H60-A knickpoint-corridor steepness with a DEM slope-magnitude filter (>median of positive set) to reduce false positives from flat-region noise. Keeps only strike-aligned, high-gradient pixels.
named_non_fault_mimic: Lithology contrast, climate-gradient steepening, ephemeral-channel base levels, or dense lattice artifacts (e.g. r13_lattice_s5 overlap). The slope filter specifically targets lithology/flat mimics.
physical_signature_targeted: Aggregate steepness step (log-ksn / chi profile step) aligned across independent drainages along a common strike; emission only where H60-A positive pixels coincide with high local slope magnitude
why_hidden_faults_rather_than_catalogue: Scarps degrade and bury; channel profiles persist. Even if individual knickpoints are sub-resolution at 100 m, aggregate strike-corridor steepness anomalies should remain. The slope filter removes catalogue-aligned false positives that don't have steep profiles.
difference_from_repo_implementations: Previous H60-A emitted uniformly across corridors (40,000 dots). H63-A applies a slope-concordance filter before emission (36,000 dots) and uses a different random seed. Previous GEMS61 used thermal concordance. This is the first slope-filtered emission in the family.
